instruction: Choose a suitable finite-element simulation tool available in the current Windows fused environment. Use a command-line or scripting workflow. Use the selected finite-element simulation tool to perform a tensile analysis of a rectangular solid block: 1. Part: - 3D Deformable Solid, Extrusion - Sketch a rectangle from (0,0) to (12,8) in the Y-Z plane - Extrude along the global X-axis to length 120 mm - This creates a block with cross-section 12 mm x 8 mm and length 120 mm 2. Property: - Material Aluminum: E = 70000 MPa, nu = 0.33 - Solid Homogeneous section 3. Assembly: Create an instance. 4. Step: - Static, General, named Step-Load 5. Load: - Fix the end face at X=0 with Encastre boundary condition - Apply a uniform pressure of 8.33 MPa on the end face at X=120 mm in the +X direction (equivalent to a total 800 N tensile force) 6. Mesh: - Global seed size: 4 mm - Element type: appropriate three-dimensional solid element formulation 7. Job: Create Job-BlockTension and submit for solving. 8. Deliverables: save the native model artifact and native solver result artifact on the Desktop, and write `C:/Users/user/Desktop/metrics.json` with numeric fields for the requested metrics.
